stories.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
summary: NASA is offering $1 million in its new Moon Base Challenge, inviting U.S. students to develop innovative solutions for building humanity’s first permanent lunar outpost.
From power systems to astronaut safety, their ideas could help make long-term life on the Moon possible and pave the way to Mars.

stories.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera has revealed a strange new world
summary: A European spacecraft has revealed a mysterious, crater-covered side of the asteroid Didymos as it prepares to investigate the aftermath of NASA’s historic 2022 asteroid impact.
The mission could uncover new clues about the collision and help turn asteroid deflection into a powerful defense against future threats to Earth.

stories.title: A hidden biological divide may help explain Alzheimer’s and chronic pain
summary: New research reveals that biological sex, genetics, and menopause may dramatically influence Alzheimer's risk, treatment responses, and chronic pain conditions such as fibromyalgia.
Scientists also uncovered surprising differences in immune activity and gut-brain interactions, opening the door to more personalized treatments for neurological disorders.

stories.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
summary: Deep beneath the Pacific Ocean, scientists have discovered tiny hidden ecosystems inside metal-rich rocks that take millions of years to form.
Researchers examined 244 nodules and found more than 4,100 animals living in their cracks and cavities, including unique communities unlike those in the surrounding seafloor mud.
These remarkable miniature habitats could now be threatened by deep-sea mining for valuable metals.

stories.title: Yellow weather warnings issued for snow as temperatures plummet
summary: A spell of colder, wintry weather will grip some northern parts of the UK, bringing a threat of ice and hill snow at times.

stories.title: Experts explore returning beavers to River Waveney
summary: A trust says the river-dwelling mammals could improve the health of the waterway.

stories.title: Pupils fascinated by space get astronomy lesson
summary: Pupils at First Tower School get a visit from a University of Cambridge astronomer.

stories.title: The secret to building Moon bases may be hiding in emergency blankets
summary: Scientists have turned the thin plastic used in emergency blankets into remarkably strong insulation that could help astronauts survive the Moon's extreme temperatures.
Built from hundreds of stacked layers, the material withstands crushing pressure without losing its thermal protection, potentially paving the way for tougher, longer-lasting lunar habitats.

stories.title: Physicists defy expectations by controlling the magnetic heart of a single atom
summary: Scientists have unexpectedly discovered how to control the magnetic spin inside a single atom's nucleus using radio waves, overturning previous assumptions about atomic behavior.
The breakthrough could pave the way for more reliable quantum memory, although researchers are still trying to understand why it works.

stories.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
summary: A virus that infected chimpanzees millions of years ago may have helped shape one of the most important differences between humans and our closest relatives: how our brains develop.

Scientists at Lund University discovered that ancient viral DNA embedded in the chimpanzee genome switches off a gene called LINC00662, which remains active in humans and appears to play an important role in early brain development.

stories.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
summary: Scientists have discovered that vitamin C may help prevent potentially cancer-causing chemicals from forming in the stomach after eating foods containing nitrates and nitrites.
A new mathematical model suggests that taking vitamin C after meals could reduce these harmful reactions, offering a possible new strategy for lowering cancer risk.

stories.title: A common osteoporosis drug blocked spinal damage in a surprising new study
summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising genetic connection to spinal degeneration and found that an existing osteoporosis drug can prevent damaging mineral buildup in zebrafish spines.
The discovery could pave the way for new treatments that slow or prevent a major cause of chronic back pain.

stories.title: Uranus and Neptune’s bizarre magnetic fields may finally be explained
summary: The strange, wildly tilted magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune have puzzled scientists since NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft explored the planets in the 1980s.
New simulations suggest that extreme conditions deep inside these icy giants create unusual electrical properties that could explain their magnetic fields.
Remarkably, the models indicate that their magnetic poles could shift by tens of degrees within just a few decades, far faster than Earth's.

stories.title: Astronomers discover a dead star spinning every 8 minutes and sending mysterious radio pulses
summary: Scientists have discovered a strange stellar pair more than 5,000 light-years away, where a dead star spinning every eight minutes produces mysterious radio pulses while orbiting a Sun-like star.
The breakthrough also revealed massive magnetic storms on the companion star, offering fresh clues to one of astronomy's emerging mysteries.

stories.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
summary: A surprising discovery from Rockefeller University suggests that a common amino acid could play a powerful role in protecting against cancer and viral infections.

Scientists found that low arginine levels interfere with the immune system's ability to recognize dangerous cells, while increasing arginine intake reduced colon cancer tumors and improved viral infection outcomes in mice.
Even more remarkably, giving mice arginine after they contracted influenza helped them recover.

stories.title: How to spot November's planetary parade in the pre-dawn sky
summary: The planets of Mercury, Venus, Mars and Jupiter will align in pre-dawn sky throughout November.
